blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Logistics networks and optimisation, at senior level, move beyond rates and contracts into the architecture of flows. How many hubs do we need? Where are the optimal routes? Which lanes are better handled in-house and which by partners? What is the carbon footprint of each choice, now that regulators and customers are asking? These questions do not have single answers — they have trade-offs.

A well-run optimisation exercise balances four things: cost, service, risk and sustainability. Cheap and fast and resilient and green almost never exist together. The senior leader's job is to decide, explicitly, which two or three the company is running for, and to live with the consequences of the others.

What distinguishes good logistics strategy from bad is not cleverness — it is explicitness. Good leaders tell the organisation: "we prioritise service and resilience; we accept a small cost penalty on the west-coast lanes." Bad leaders pretend they are running for all four at once, and then wonder why nothing is actually optimised.

items.q: According to the text, at senior level logistics moves beyond rates and contracts into…
items.why: "…move beyond rates and contracts into the architecture of flows."

items.q: Which four things does a well-run optimisation exercise balance?
items.why: "balances four things: cost, service, risk and sustainability."

items.q: The text says the difference between good and bad logistics strategy is…
items.why: "…is not cleverness — it is explicitness."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Leaders should say out loud which priorities they accept losing.
Every design choice carries a trade-off.
The carbon footprint of a route now matters to regulators.
A network can be optimised for cost, speed, resilience and sustainability all at once.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que barato, rápido, resiliente e verde quase nunca coexistem — quem finge otimizar os quatro é o "bad leader".

items.q: The example "we accept a small cost penalty on the west-coast lanes" suggests that…
options: cost was chosen as the top priority
a good leader names what is being sacrificed, not just what is prioritised
the west-coast lanes should be outsourced
items.why: Inferência: o exemplo mostra a explicitação — assumir abertamente a consequência (o custo maior) da prioridade escolhida.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver apresentando o novo desenho da rede logística. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, before I walk you through the map, let me be completely explicit about what we are optimising for — because that decision drives everything else.

For the North American network, we are running for service and resilience. Not the lowest possible cost. I want that on the record. We are consolidating from five hubs down to three, which is considerably cheaper to operate, but a leaner network is inherently more fragile — so we are deliberately keeping a fourth, smaller hub in the interior purely as a resilience buffer. It costs us money. I am recommending we spend it.

On the west-coast lanes, we accept a small cost penalty. Those lanes are significantly more time-sensitive, and the shorter transit time frees up working capital that more than pays for the premium. In-house on the core lanes, partners on the long tail.

And to be clear — this is never finished. As trade patterns shift, we revisit it. What I am not going to do is stand here and pretend we have squeezed cost, speed, resilience and carbon all at the same time. We haven't. We chose two.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Oliver explicitly optimising the North American network for?
items.why: "we are running for service and resilience. Not the lowest possible cost."

items.q: Why is Oliver keeping a fourth, smaller hub in the interior?
items.why: "keeping a fourth, smaller hub in the interior purely as a resilience buffer."

items.q: According to Oliver, what justifies the cost penalty on the west-coast lanes?
options: The lanes have the lowest volume
Shorter transit time frees up working capital
items.why: "the shorter transit time frees up working capital that more than pays for the premium."

items.q: What does Oliver mean by "a leaner network is inherently more fragile"?
options: Concentrating the network reduces cost but raises risk
Fewer hubs cost more to run
Partners are less reliable than in-house teams
items.why: Inferência: consolidar de cinco para três hubs barateia, mas remove folga — daí o buffer de resiliência.

items.q: How would you best describe Oliver's stance?
options: Honest about the trade-offs, refusing to claim he optimised everything
Confident he has minimised cost, speed and carbon together
Reluctant to commit to any priority
items.why: Inferência: ele recusa fingir que espremeu tudo — "We chose two" — assumindo abertamente o que abriu mão.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Every design choice is a trade-off." A trade-off is…
options: a benefit gained by accepting a corresponding loss
a guaranteed improvement on all fronts
items.why: Trade-off = compromisso: ganhar em um ponto aceitando perder em outro.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We consolidated from five ___ to three to lower operating cost."
items.why: Hub = ponto de concentração da rede; consolidar hubs reduz custo.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The west-coast ___ are time-sensitive, so we route them differently."
items.why: Lane = rota/corredor de transporte específico.

items.q: Carbon footprint is best described as…
options: the greenhouse-gas impact of a choice
the total distance a shipment travels
the cost of fuel per lane
the number of hubs in a network
items.why: Carbon footprint = pegada de carbono: o impacto em emissões que reguladores e clientes passaram a exigir.

items.q: "We accept a small cost penalty on those lanes." A cost penalty is…
options: a fine imposed by a regulator
a discount negotiated with a partner
the extra cost accepted in exchange for another priority
items.why: Cost penalty = penalidade de custo: o custo adicional que se aceita para ganhar em serviço ou resiliência.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de estratégia logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the new network design." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new hub structure region by region." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Consolidating to three hubs won't move the needle on carbon." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "Two regional heads pushed back on closing the interior hub." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed the resilience plan but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.
